column1: # testees/pcrec/list_limits.tsv -- pcrec's NUMERIC-LIMITS TABLE at the pin
# docs/spec/table_contract.md), archived VERBATIM under a source header --
# the THIRD archive target beside list_axes.tsv / list_definitions.tsv
# (inbox I-25: "ARCHIVE IT beside --list-axes at your re-pin"). Everything
# below this header is the unmodified output of:
# 2026-08-31 by lane b22repin ([B22]). 44 data rows / 7 columns (name,
# value, unit, kind, override, anchor, desc) -- one row per numeric limit
# in pcrec src/core/limits.def, in the table's own order; FIRST archive of
# this surface (the table is new at this pin -- I-25's 44 rows, measured
# 44). The rows this bench has already met by name:
# forms overflow by -- I-22/I-23's distinct `_WHY` route),
# 3072 (the stamped default capacities the `_in` testees exist for).
# WHAT THIS FILE IS FOR: nothing the adapter reads depends on it today (the
# caps and capacities it needs are STAMPED per artifact and read from the
# artifact, never from this table); it is archived so a limit pcrec moves
# between pins is a named diff here rather than an unexplained selection
# or refusal change in a record, and `make check-harness` diffs it against
# the pin's live output (`check_list_limits_registry`). NOT a limits row:
# the [OPT-5] letters/digits selection split (inbox I-26: the deciding
# variable is run-time-only, no selection-knee row will be added).
# Re-archive at every re-pin: the diff is the list of what moved.
# SIXTH TSV surface; D90/[LIM-1]). One row per numeric limit in
# src/core/limits.def, in the table's own order.
# unit: the quantity's dimension, or empty for a dimensionless
# kind: "compile budget" (bounds the COMPILER's own analysis or
#   emission; crossing it can refuse a pattern) | "runtime
#   capacity" (bounds the EMITTED MATCHER's own resource use;
#   crossing it is a give-up, never a wrong answer) | "size cap"
#   threshold or default that steers a selection mechanism, not a
#   hard ceiling) | "identifier cap" (bounds a name's length or a
# override: "flag" (a CLI flag or pcrec_options field moves it per
#   compile) | "-D" (only a build-time -D at pcrec's OWN compile
# anchor: the docs/spec/limits.md section this number is
#   documented in, empty when it is not (limits.md states caller-
#   facing PROMISES, not an internals catalogue — see this file's
#   own header and src/core/limits.def's for the boundary).

K38: fixed buffer size for every emitted identifier/sub-expression built from the -p prefix

[M4.7b]/K7: total NFA-state-list elements the priority subset construction may intern, summed over both machines
[M4.5b]: the VM emitter's own node-count size backstop
[M4.5c]: how many times a bounded repeat may replicate a body with a choice point
[K22]: total replication product along a chain of nested bounded repeats — a literal alias of PCREC_MAX_VM_NODES, not tuned separately
[ENG-BREP]: the counter rung's default unroll factor K, overridden by --unroll=N
[ENG-BREP]: byte-consuming positions a quantifier body may have before possessify.c declines it
[ENG-BREP]: capturing groups a quantifier body may contain before revdet.c declines the reverse-deterministic rung
[OPT-ALTCLS] stage 2: how deep prefix factoring may recurse into a group that just split
FIX-1/K5: the largest {n,m} quantifier count PCRE2 accepts (measured against libpcre2 10.46)
PCRE2's own nested-group depth ceiling (measured); also bounds parser/AST recursion depth
[M6.3]: a named group's name, measured against libpcre2 10.46 (PCRE2 error 148 above it)
a (*VERB) name; PCRE2-internals tier, measured over both name tables
(*LIMIT_MATCH=N) and friends: the accumulator magnitude PCRE2 refuses at (UINT32_MAX/10 - 1)
\p{...}/\P{...} property name, in SIGNIFICANT characters (measured against libpcre2 10.46)
[DD-14 wave G]: per-call-site AST-node splice budget before a call linkage is forced
[DD-14 wave G]: total added AST nodes across every spliced call site in one compile
[ENG-ABS]: the optional anchored match-here machine's own DFA state ceiling, lower than the mandatory pair's

[M4.6a]: trail's own clamp ceiling, paired with VM_MAX_AUTO_RESUME_FRAMES
